competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move. Supported STIR contracts use exchange DV01 and currency conversion; historical rows without that stamp keep the legacy duration-one vintage and are not silently restated. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: Overnight markets stayed defensive: the S&P 500 closed at 7416.59, gold held near 3853, and Treasuries found a modest bid while short-end yields remain elevated after a multi-day backup of roughly 26–32 basis points. WTI settled at 85.72 and Brent at 92.44, in line with crude slipping toward $85 as Middle East exports recover even as Hormuz tensions intensified with a tanker strike and a third U.S. carrier in the region. The dollar firmed against G10; USD/JPY sat at 159.60 near a five-year extreme and USDCAD pressed a five-year high. Euro-area resilience and firm U.S. activity keep ECB hike pricing in focus, while Chair Warsh’s warnings on AI disappointment added to risk sentiment. Watch Australia wages and labour force, euro-area HICP, Japan CPI, Canada retail trade, U.S. retail sales already in the tape, later PCE, income and GDP, plus Bank of Canada, RBNZ, and the FOMC.

lifecycle.realization_logic: The book earns the 146 basis point gap by receiving the US two-year at 4.83 and paying the Canada two-year at 3.37, provided that gap does not collapse.

carry-is-king.invalidation: Exit the US-versus-Canada two-year receive if the US two-year yield falls into the Canada two-year yield, or if CORRA March 2027 reprices up through SOFR March 2027 and the policy gap disappears.
carry-is-king.thesis: Close the 25 million long CORRA March 2027 and open 20 million receiving the US two-year against paying the Canada two-year. Live CORRA March 2027 at 2.955 is through the 2.995 entry, so the receive is ahead, but it still sits far under SOFR March 2027 at 4.58 while the Canada strip keeps rising. The replacement is the 146 basis point gap between the US two-year at 4.83 and the Canada two-year at 3.37. Dollar-yen carries a larger yield gap but spot is already elevated at 159.60.

expression_memo.rationale: No STIR, cash tenor, or spot has a contract that is both openable and missing the step. December SOFR is the expression just closed, and euro and kiwi have already moved.

causal.assumptions_right: The ticket named the producer-price release as the catalyst and named 4.295 as the level that made the pay wrong. Settlement at 4.2975 is that line, not a break through it.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The pay assumed the larger December step was still missing from the December contract. The two-year already held the hike, so the producer-price release had no remaining gap to close in December SOFR.
causal.causal_divergence: The position required the producer-price release to lift the December implied yield. What printed was a non-move: December settled at 4.2975, on the 4.295 line, while the hike sat in the two-year.
causal.future_implication: A policy step the two-year already holds is not a path through the December meeting contract. The next rates expression has to be a different contract, in front of a print that is not already inside the recent backup.
causal.observed_reality: The contract did not travel between the 12 November open and the 16 November close. Fresh December settlement is 4.2975, essentially on the 4.295 invalidation, cash SOFR is 3.90, and the close was taken because the two-year already held the hike.
causal.original_belief: The short December 2026 SOFR would gain if the December implied yield rose, because the December meeting was marked for a larger step than the contract already priced and the producer-price release would extend the consumer-price rise into that remark.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: On the information available at the close, December at 4.2975, cash SOFR at 3.90, no travel in the contract, and the two-year already holding the hike, the indicated action was the close that was taken.

postmortems.future_rule: Do not pay a dated SOFR meeting contract unless that contract, rather than the two-year, is where the step is missing. If the meeting contract has not traveled off its invalidation and the two-year already holds the hike, close it and do not reopen it on the same catalyst.
postmortems.lesson: A front SOFR pay is the wrong expression when the two-year already holds the hike and the meeting contract is sitting on its invalidation.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The book gained only if the December implied yield rose because the December meeting was marked for a larger step than the contract priced. That rise did not occur.
postmortems.what_failed: The expression failed. December 2026 SOFR did not reprice, because the larger meeting step the short was paid to capture was already held by the two-year, and the contract finished at 4.2975 on its 4.295 line.

causal.assumptions_right: The September contract was cheap to cash and the implied rate did rise from about 4.71 to 4.815, so the narrow mechanism that a priced cut would be reduced operated in the direction of the pay.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The entry equated removal of one cut with a hiking cycle that would take September through cash, but the RBA can set a higher near-term rate and still ease by late 2027, which is the path March at 4.92 versus September at 4.815 was already describing.
causal.causal_divergence: The level moved in favor of the pay because part of the embedded cut came out, but the mechanism required to finish the move through cash was a path with no residual easing, and the strip delivered a higher March fixing while September remained below both March and cash.
causal.future_implication: A new September AONIA pay is warranted only if September implied trades above cash and the March-September spread stops pricing later cuts. Until then the hawkish Australian information sits in the front of the strip.
causal.observed_reality: The pay was opened on 10 November and closed on 16 November, and the fresh September 2027 settlement is 4.815, higher than the entry area but still short of cash, while March 2027 AONIA at 4.92 is already above that cash rate.
causal.original_belief: September 2027 AONIA near 4.71 embedded an RBA cut versus cash near 4.85, so paying that contract would work as the cut was removed and the implied rate was pulled back through the cash rate.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same entry information the position should have been a cut-removal pay with a curve-shape exit: once March was above cash and September was still below cash, the back-contract pay should have been closed rather than held for a print through cash.

postmortems.future_rule: Exit a back-contract policy pay when the preceding contract is already above cash and the back contract remains below cash, because that curve is residual easing and not an unfinished hike.
postmortems.lesson: Removing one priced cut and starting a hiking cycle are different policy paths, and the March-versus-September AONIA spread is the market's statement of which path is priced.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The pay correctly identified a cut that was too large in September 2027 AONIA, and implied rose from about 4.71 to a 4.815 settlement, but it wrongly treated that removal as a hiking cycle that would carry the contract through cash near 4.85.
postmortems.what_failed: The claim that deleting one priced cut would reprice September as the hiking-cycle contract failed, because the strip lifted March 2027 to 4.92 and left September at 4.815, still under cash.
